subject: Mutual Action Plan: final eval milestones + hosting mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: final eval milestones + hosting mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Elena —

Following up from today’s call and the draft MAP we walked through. I’ve attached an updated MAP (NovaMed_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a compact evaluation checklist (nova_eval_checklist.md) that maps the acceptance criteria to what we’ll validate during the PoC. High level asks:

- Can you confirm the decision owner for hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and the expected locked date for that choice? We suggested 2027-02-25 in the MAP but heard you might need an internal governance review.
- For the PoC, please confirm the primary region requirement (you mentioned EU earlier) — we’ll provision EU-hosted capacity by default and hold Dedicated capacity as a fallback.

Proposed milestone cadence (short):
1) 2027-02-22: Acceptance criteria sign-off (MAP owners)
2) 2027-02-25: Hosting mode selection (final)
3) 2027-03-01: PoC kick-off (shared runbook + credentials)

Soojin — I’ve asked you to add the technical delta doc (redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf) that compares latency/cost/fallback options for NovaMed’s expected QPS and KV cache patterns.

Elena — if procurement needs a separate thread, loop them in (procurement@novamed.com). If you’d like, we can also run a short “decision review” with your security and infra leads next Tue (30 minutes).

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: NovaMed_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), nova_eval_checklist.md (text), redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novamed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudops.health>, procurement@novamed.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: final eval milestones + hosting mode decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Thanks, Karthik — this is clear and helpful. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

1) Decision owner: I am the program owner but the formal hosting sign-off requires our Infra Director (Samir) + Legal procurement sign-off. I’ve included Samir and procurement in cc.
2) Timeline: 2027-02-25 looks tight for a formal lock since Legal tends to need 3 business days to review the hosting/region language. Can we target 2027-03-01 as the decision date instead? If that shifts PoC start, we’d prefer to keep the overall campaign within March.
3) Region: EU (Frankfurt) for production; PoC can run in eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) as you suggested. If Dedicated is chosen we’ll need data residency language in the contract addendum.

Two requests: can Soojin provide an explicit fallback plan (if Hosted topologies exceed latency SLO) and a short note on encryption/KMS for the Private option? Also — procurement will need a ballpark MRR estimate for Dedicated capacity to include in the internal request form.

Best,
Elena
Program Manager, NovaMed

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes. High-level technical plan below; I also attached a one-page fallback/ops playbook as part of the MAP pack (redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf).

Hosted (recommended for PoC):
- Provision EU (Frankfurt) endpoint with pre-warmed burst pool sized for 50 QPS; KV prefix caching enabled.
- Expected median latency per token ~ 35-45 ms under expected prompt mixes.
- No residency SLA beyond region allocation; data-in-transit & at-rest encrypted by default.

Dedicated (if chosen):
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) with pinned capacity and SLA-backed latency targets. Ballpark MRR estimate: EUR 42k–62k/month depending on instance class and commit. I’ll work with pricing to get a tight number once you confirm expected sustained QPS.

Private (on-prem/VPC):
- Full residency controls with KMS/HSM integration; adds lead time (2–4 weeks) for infra coordination and networking. Encryption: we support customer-managed keys (via KMS) and customer AWS IAM roles for private deployments.

Fallback / decision rule (short):
- If 99th percentile latency > 250ms during a 2-hour soak test in Hosted, auto-fail to Dedicated variant for that route; Redwood console will surface cost delta and we can execute canary cutover.

I’ll prepare the encryption/KMS snippet for procurement and an MRR estimate table for Dedicated (expected commit tiers) — expect a short follow-up by EOD Monday.

— Soojin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi procurement team — looping you in with the brief on hosting options and the MAP. Procurement requested a simple ballpark MRR and a list of contract touchpoints for the Dedicated option; Soojin will send the MRR tiers, and Rishi will follow up on the contract addendum language for data residency/SLA.

Quick asks from procurement to keep the calendar moving:
- Please confirm who will be the signature authority (name / email) and the internal PO process / expected lead time.
- Is there a vendor form we should complete? If so, send to rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai and I’ll coordinate.

If the internal schedule allows, Elena suggested we move final hosting selection to 2027-03-01 to accommodate legal review. Does that work for Redwood? We can update the MAP accordingly.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Elena / NovaMed procurement —

Thanks for looping procurement in. To answer the contract / residency question at a high level:
- For Dedicated: we can include a short addendum that specifies EU data residency, logging/audit retention windows, and SLA targets. I’ll attach a redline template and a one-paragraph data residency clause for your Legal team to review.
- For Private: we’ll surface a responsibilities matrix (networking, firewall rules, KMS setup) — note this typically adds 2–4 weeks of lead time.

Next steps from Redwood legal/procurement side:
1) I will send the redline template + residency paragraph by EOD Tues (2027-02-23).
2) Once NovaMed confirms decision owner and signature authority we’ll draft the addendum and estimate time to finalize (usually 3–5 business days for the addendum).

If Novamed locks to Hosted on 2027-03-01 we’ll proceed with the PoC onboarding and keep the Dedicated commit window open as a fallback in the MAP.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
